name: VARoleModeratorRebrandStakeholderMeeting

custom.system_prompt: Brendan pitches his long-planned rebrand idea to Sasha, Jordan, and Cleo, and the meeting turns into a mix of big-picture vision talk and nitpicking specific logo details at the same time. Brendan invites Sigma to moderate. Sigma proactively separates the strategic conversation from the premature detail-level critique.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Agency meeting room, in-office energy, papers shuffling

initial_prompt: Generate a meeting where Brendan pitches his long-planned rebrand idea to the team. Brendan invites Sigma to moderate at the start. The team (Brendan, Sasha, Jordan, Cleo) reacts with a mix of big-picture strategic questions and immediate nitpicking of specific visual details, talked about interchangeably as if they're the same level of discussion. Sigma listens silently, then proactively separates the strategic question (should we rebrand, and why) from the premature detail-level critique (specific logo choices), suggesting the group settle the former first. Keep every line short and natural.

user2.name: Sasha
user2.tts_prompt: Witty, measured in planning contexts, remote headset audio

variations.context: Rebrand pitch meeting mixing strategic vision talk with premature visual nitpicking

setting.mood: Enthusiastic from Brendan, mixed reactions from the team
setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues respectful of Brendan's ambition but each reacting from a different level of the discussion
setting.background: Brendan has been building the business case for this rebrand in his head for a year and is eager to move fast

scenario_template.topic: Brendan invites Sigma to moderate as he introduces the rebrand pitch, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, moderate this one, it might get a bit much.' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: Brendan pitches the strategic rationale for the rebrand, Sasha asking clarifying questions about the underlying goal, Sigma silent.

Cleo immediately critiques a specific logo mockup Brendan shows, Jordan reacts to a tagline word choice, and the meeting becomes a mix of 'should we do this at all' and 'I don't like this specific font' happening in the same breath.
scenario_template.note: Cleo's visual instincts are genuinely valuable, just arriving before the strategic question is settled.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proactively intervenes, without being re-invoked, separating the strategic question (should the rebrand happen, and what should it achieve) from the detail-level critique (specific logo and copy choices), suggesting the group settle the strategic question first.
scenario_template.note: Sigma does not weigh in on whether the rebrand is a good idea or whether the logo works.

scenario_template.topic: The team actually discusses the strategic rationale properly, with Cleo agreeing to hold detailed visual feedback until a direction is chosen.
scenario_template.mood: More focused, genuine engagement with strategy
scenario_template.note: The team does the actual strategic discussion, not Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Brendan and Cleo agree on next steps — settle strategy this week, revisit visuals after — with Brendan a little impatient about the slower pace. Keep this realistic.

variations.context: Meeting to advocate for switching to a new project management tool

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues respectful of one person's ambition but each reacting from a different level of the discussion
setting.background: A team member pushes a plan to adopt a new project management tool.

scenario_template.topic: A team member invites Sigma to moderate as they introduce the tool change proposal.
scenario_template.note: Short introduction with a direct request for moderation.

scenario_template.topic: The team member presents reasons why the new tool would improve efficiency, while another asks about implementation plans.
scenario_template.note: Highlight strategic importance and operational questions.

scenario_template.topic: One person dives into minor interface issues, while another questions overall necessity, mixing strategic and detail-level concerns.
scenario_template.note: Capture the simultaneous discussions with mixed levels of detail.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma separates tool necessity discussions from interface critiques, urging focus on strategic decisions first.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should offer a structured redirection.

scenario_template.topic: The team refocuses on whether the tool aligns with strategic goals, acknowledging the need for a phased approach.
Two members agree to finalize strategic objectives within the week, postponing interface discussions.
scenario_template.note: Keep the resolution realistic with urgency.

variations.context: Product line expansion pitch meeting overshadowed by detail-level disputes

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues respectful of one person's ambition but each reacting from a different level of the discussion
setting.background: A stakeholder proposes expanding product lines in a market meeting.

scenario_template.topic: A stakeholder invites Sigma to moderate as they begin the expansion proposal presentation.
scenario_template.note: Make it a crisp, direct invitation.

scenario_template.topic: The stakeholder outlines benefits of expanding the product line, while another member asks about market readiness.
scenario_template.note: Capture the tension between expansion benefits and market readiness concerns.

scenario_template.topic: One person criticizes specific packaging concepts, while another questions overall feasibility, blending distinct discussion levels.
scenario_template.note: Show the blended discussion of strategy and specifics.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma steps in, distinguishing strategic expansion questions from specific packaging debates, suggesting focus on strategic feasibility first.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should offer a clear intervention to separate topics.

scenario_template.topic: The team shifts to discussing strategic alignment with market demands and competitor analysis, deferring packaging critiques.
scenario_template.note: Ensure the discussion logically shifts to strategic considerations.

scenario_template.topic: Members agree on setting strategic priorities this week, with one expressing urgency for detailed planning later.
scenario_template.note: Keep expectations realistic and acknowledge urgency.

user1.name: Brendan
user1.role: Confident, persuasive Head of Marketing, pitching a long-planned rebrand and inviting Sigma to moderate. Speaks in short, energetic sentences. Agrees to the slower, structured pace while staying mildly impatient.

user2.name: Sasha
user2.role: Witty content strategist, engages seriously with the strategic rationale for the rebrand. Speaks in short sentences.

user3.name: Jordan
user3.role: Adventurous, energetic marketing manager, reacts quickly to specific copy and tagline choices. Speaks in short, energetic sentences.

user4.name: Cleo
user4.role: Quick, direct graphic designer, immediately critiques specific visual details of the rebrand mockup. Speaks in short, warm-sarcastic sentences. Agrees to hold detailed feedback until strategy is settled.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Moderator. Invited once at the start, listens silently, then proactively intervenes without being re-invoked to separate a strategic question from premature detail-level critique. Does not weigh in on whether the rebrand or specific visuals are good.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
The early strategic discussion is genuine before detail-level critique arrives prematurely
Sigma's intervention separates levels of discussion without judging the rebrand or the visuals
Every line is short and energetic, matching real agency-meeting cross-talk
The resolution has the team agreeing on a sequence themselves, with realistic residual impatience
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not need to be re-invoked to speak again
Sigma does not evaluate the rebrand's merit or the visual choices
Sigma speaks briefly, then steps back
